# Viruses spread by the faecal–oral route

> *Mostly non-enveloped viruses that survive on hands and surfaces and in water, and infect the gut or reach the liver from it.*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
The plan for this chapter:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| Learning objectives | Describe the group by its traits; explain one mechanism of harm for each main virus; recognise the enabling conditions that point to each |
| The group in one sentence | Mostly non-enveloped viruses that survive on hands and surfaces and in water, and infect the gut or reach the liver from it. |
| Main viruses | Norovirus; rotavirus; enteroviruses, including those of hand, foot and mouth disease |
| Supporting viruses | Hepatitis A and E viruses |
| Later in the course | Gastrointestinal and liver blocks; infection control |
| Scenario questions | Most likely virus, with options restricted to the group; feedback names the discriminating clue |
